title: Yermak's Siberian campaign
summary: The Cossack ataman Yermak, hired by the Stroganov merchants, led a few hundred men by boat along Siberian rivers in 1582. After defeating Khan Kuchum he occupied the khan's capital Kashlyk (Isker) in October 1582 and received tribute from local peoples. Kuchum later killed most of the band, but later expeditions continued the Russian annexation of Siberia.

uncertainty.note: The start of the expedition is dated 1581 by most sources and 1582 by Skrynnikov (Encyclopedia.com); the occupation of Kashlyk is October 1582.

where.modern_name: Isker (Qashliq) fortress site near Tobolsk, Tyumen Oblast, Russia
where.historical_name: Kashlyk (Isker, Sibir), capital of Khan Kuchum's Khanate of Sibir

importance.justification: The campaign began the Russian annexation of Siberia.

sources.title: How Siberia was once a separate country

reviewer_note: Encyclopedia.com says many details are disputed: the start year (1581 or 1582), the size of the force and who ordered the offensive. Only "a few hundred" and 1582 are used. The pin is the Isker fortress site, not a route.
